# user_dialog HTTP store header lifecycle goldens

Node v22.22.0 (macOS arm64) raw-socket captures for issue #699.

- `node-408.bin` — 51 bytes, `_http_server.js` `requestTimeoutResponse`
  (`HTTP/1.1 408 Request Timeout\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n`). Captured from a
  real `node:http` server and from the real TS entry
  `startGatewayUserDialogStoreHttpServer` (no options) for both a zero-byte
  connection and a partial request head at 90,000 ms.
- `node-431.bin` — 67 bytes, `requestHeaderFieldsTooLargeResponse`
  (`HTTP/1.1 431 Request Header Fields Too Large\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n`).
  Both are whitespace-exact: capital `Connection`, no `content-length`, no
  `date`.
- `node-matrix-default.json` — default timers (`headersTimeout` 60 s,
  `connectionsCheckingInterval` 30 s, `keepAliveTimeout` 5 s + 1 s). Generated by
  `_tmp/20261025-issue-699/node/probe-header-lifecycle.mjs`; full raw bytes are
  the `hex`/`text` fields of each cell.
- `node-matrix-short.json` — same server with explicit
  `headersTimeout=300 ms`, `requestTimeout=300 ms`,
  `connectionsCheckingInterval=50 ms` (and per-case `keepAliveTimeout`s), so the
  same byte constants are observable for follow-up/shutdown/body cells. Generated
  by `_tmp/20261025-issue-699/node/probe-header-lifecycle-short.mjs`.

Key timing facts (do not normalize away):

- default zero-byte and partial first head: 51-byte 408 at 90,000 ms
  (`node-matrix-default.json`, `elapsedMs` 90001 / 90000);
- default single partial *follow-up* head: silent EOF at ~6,049 ms because
  `keepAliveTimeout + buffer` fires before `headersTimeout`; a follow-up head
  that keeps the socket active gets the 51-byte 408 at the header deadline
  (`short-keepalive-partial-header-wins`, 300 ms class);
- default oversized head: 67-byte 431 in <50 ms, then EOF;
- 15,000-byte under-limit control: 200 (167 bytes), not 431;
- body `requestTimeout` with short timers: the same 51-byte 408
  (`short-body-timeout`, 308 ms);
- `server.close()` destroys idle keep-alive connections (0 extra bytes) and
  idle pre-parser connections, but after the parser has consumed a partial head
  it neither destroys nor lets the checker fire (the checker interval is
  cleared by `close()`), so that connection hangs until the peer closes. Rust
  closes header-phase connections promptly and never fabricates a 408 on
  shutdown; see the difference note in `RESULT.md`.

`date` values and ephemeral ports are runtime-dependent; the byte fixtures are
the only exact goldens compared in Rust tests.
